title: The Freezer Role can revoke a Relayer but never grant one, so emergency power can only subtract
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.1.2 states the asymmetry precisely: "the Relayer Role may be granted to an address by any address holding the `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`. The Relayer Role may be removed from an address by any address holding the `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` **or** the `FREEZER_ROLE`." A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.1.4 then defines the freezer minimally: "the address of the emergency role that can remove a compromised Relayer."

This is what makes a low-threshold emergency role safe to hand to a fast-moving group. A compromised or captured Freezer Multisig cannot install an operator of its choosing, cannot move funds, and cannot grant itself anything — its entire capability is destructive. The worst outcome of freezer capture is a halted Liquidity Layer, which is also the *intended* outcome of legitimate use.

The general principle is worth extracting: emergency authority should be monotonic in the safe direction. Any role that can both add and remove privileges is as dangerous as the privileges it manages, whereas a subtract-only role can be given a 2-of-5 threshold and still not be a route to theft.

It also clarifies the division with the admin. Recovery — restoring a relayer after a freeze — requires `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which sits with Sky Governance. Stopping is cheap and fast; restarting is deliberately expensive and slow.
description: RELAYER_ROLE may be granted solely by DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, while either the admin or the FREEZER_ROLE can remove it — the freezer is defined as the role that removes a compromised relayer.
